title: The Revolutionaries Release Date: Bhuvan Bam Freedom Struggle Series Premieres September 11 on Prime Video
excerpt: Nikkhil Advani's period drama based on Sanjeev Sanyal's book stars Bhuvan Bam, Rohit Saraf, and Pratibha Ranta as young Indian freedom fighters.
body:
• Prime Video has confirmed September 11, 2026, as the worldwide premiere date for The Revolutionaries
  • The series is based on Sanjeev Sanyal's book and stars Bhuvan Bam, Rohit Saraf, Pratibha Ranta, Gurfateh Pirzada, and Jason Shah
  • Directed by Nikkhil Advani, the period drama was filmed across Mumbai, Amritsar, Varanasi, and Dehradun and will stream in over 240 countries

Prime Video has announced September 11, 2026, as the worldwide premiere date for The Revolutionaries, Nikkhil Advani's period drama centered on young Indian freedom fighters who championed armed resistance against British colonial rule. The series will stream exclusively on the platform across more than 240 countries and territories.

The announcement comes just days after India's 80th Independence Day celebrations, adding a timely resonance to a show that dramatizes a lesser-told chapter of the nation's freedom struggle.

A Fresh Take on India's Independence Movement

Adapted from Sanjeev Sanyal's acclaimed book Revolutionaries: The Other Story of How India Won Its Freedom, the series shifts focus from the widely depicted nonviolent resistance movement to the young rebels who believed picking up arms was the only way to end British rule. The show explores the lives and sacrifices of figures including Bhagat Singh, Subhas Chandra Bose, Aurobindo Ghosh, and Vinayak Savarkar through a dramatized narrative.

"Sanjeev Sanyal's powerful book has given us a compelling foundation to tell the untold stories of these extraordinary young patriots."

— Nikkhil Advani, Director

The series stars Bhuvan Bam, Rohit Saraf, Pratibha Ranta, Gurfateh Pirzada, Jason Shah, and Pratik Motwani. For Bhuvan Bam — best known as the creator of the YouTube comedy channel BB Ki Vines — the role marks a dramatic departure. His clean-shaven, intense look in the first-look promos sparked immediate buzz when they were released in July 2025.

Cast Transformations and Grand Production

Rohit Saraf, who rose to prominence with Mismatched, underwent significant physical training for his role as a determined revolutionary. Pratibha Ranta, celebrated for her performance in Laapataa Ladies, plays a fierce female freedom fighter in what could be her most demanding role yet.

Produced by Monisha Advani and Madhu Bhojwani under the banner of Emmay Entertainment, the series was filmed on a grand scale across multiple Indian cities — Mumbai, Amritsar, Varanasi, and Dehradun — with principal photography wrapping in November 2025. The production team recreated period-accurate settings, from rustic training grounds to colonial-era cityscapes, to capture the era with authenticity.

Nikhil Madhok, an executive at Prime Video backing the project, called it "one of their most meaningful projects yet," praising how deeply committed the cast has been to bringing real emotion and depth to their roles.

Why Diaspora Audiences Are Watching

For Indian diaspora viewers worldwide, the series lands at a moment of renewed interest in India's independence history — particularly the stories of young revolutionaries often overshadowed by the Gandhian nonviolence narrative. The global availability across 240-plus countries ensures NRI audiences from the United States to the United Kingdom, Canada, and the Gulf can stream the show from day one.

The series also joins a broader wave of Indian historical content on OTT platforms, following projects like Emmay Entertainment's own Freedom at Midnight on SonyLIV, which covered the partition era. With Advani at the helm of both, The Revolutionaries promises a complementary but distinct perspective on the independence movement.

What to Expect

The series is expected to unfold across a single season, though the episode count has not been confirmed. Character promos offering a first detailed glimpse of the main cast and the historical figures they portray have begun rolling out ahead of the September 11 premiere.

With a story that blends historical drama, action, and emotional depth, The Revolutionaries is positioned to be one of Prime Video's marquee Indian originals for 2026.
